title: Callvale before: the sign-in flood reaches the application
claim: Without a web ACL, the sign-in flood reaches the application.
alt: Before: sign-in requests pass CloudFront and the load balancer to the application. The application reaches any domain through NAT gateways.

edges.say: Sign-in requests from many addresses reach CloudFront.
No web ACL checks them at CloudFront or the load balancer.
Workloads reach any domain through the NAT gateways.

notes: Brief 08 story pair, 2-deep.md#decision-record (after Context). Caption from brief.json; the steps state no AWS rule. Same cells as edge-protection-after: flood A1, CloudFront A2, load balancer A3, application A4, NAT gateway A6, internet A7. The 'No web ACL' boxes in B2, B3 become the web ACLs; the empty A5 becomes the firewall endpoint; B1 stays empty for Firewall Manager. One Availability Zone drawn. The highlight is the flood's path. No AWS number in the drawing.
